outcome: A person records the project retrospective as a saved version and sees where it stands in the closure checklist
acceptance_criteria: Case 2001 on Next 4990 + mock 4991 at `/projects/<2001>/retrospective?dossier=5001` shows the project title, three empty boxes, Who took part, Notes file, "Save retrospective" and no "Save draft" anywhere. — verify: open the page; search the page text and `src/features/retrospective` for "draft" (none).

Saving with only "What went well" filled, one participant, a notes file and a time sends one `POST /api/v1/projects/<case>/meetings` whose body has `kind:"retrospective"`, `meeting_id:null`, the current `revision`, a `reference`, and a `summary` that is exactly `## What went well\n<text>` — verify: network panel / Playwright request assertion; then the page shows "Saved ... version 1" only after the re-read.
Saving with all three boxes sends them in the order went well, didn't, lessons, each under its heading, joined by one blank line — verify: unit test on `summary.ts` and the e2e request body.

Parsing: a `summary` with the three headings fills the three boxes; one with no headings (case 2002 v1) shows as a single "Retrospective" block and saving it unchanged sends the identical text; a heading in different case or with a curly apostrophe still parses; text before the first heading appears under "Other notes" — verify: unit tests in `summary.test.ts` including a round trip.
Saving again on case 2002 sends `meeting_id:301` and the same `reference` (read-only field) and the page then shows version 3 — verify: e2e request body and page.

Case 2002 with `dossier=5002`: the strip shows "The checklist used version 1" with its date, and "A newer version has been saved. The checklist has not picked it up yet."; no request carries a "latest" filter or `retrospective_id` — verify: e2e and request log.
`/projects/<2002>/retrospective?meeting=301&version=9001` shows "Version 1, not the current version" with no Save new version button and no action controls — verify: e2e.
A stale save (mock 409) shows "This changed while you were editing. Reload and try again.", re-reads, and keeps every typed box, participant and proof — verify: e2e.
A duplicate reference (mock 422 with `fields`) shows the message under the Reference field, not as a generic error; Save re-enables — verify: e2e.

A forced 503 after sending shows "We couldn't confirm it saved", re-reads the list, and keeps Save disabled until the re-read returns; there is no automatic second POST (exactly one POST in the request log) — verify: e2e.
Double click on Save sends one POST — verify: e2e request count.

Save is disabled with the reason shown when no box has text, when no notes file is chosen, when the joined summary exceeds 16000 characters, or when `proofs` is empty (case 2004 shows "No supporting file is recorded for this project yet...") — verify: unit and e2e.

A decision row needs text and a supporting file; saving a new version loads the previous version's decisions and sends them unchanged when untouched, including any `change_evidence_id` — verify: unit test on the body builder; e2e on case 2002.

"Make this a follow-up action" sends one `POST /actions/create` with `meeting_id` and no call to `/meetings/{id}/actions`; empty deadline sends `due_at:null` and the new row reads "No deadline set"; an empty owner reads "No owner"; a duplicate action reference shows the 422 under Reference — verify: e2e request log and page.
Wrong user: case 2003 (`can_record:false`, options 403) shows saved versions read-only with no form and no action button; the 403 from options is not shown as an error — verify: e2e.
Wrong tenant or unknown case shows only "This record is unavailable." for both 404 on project read and on meetings — verify: e2e on an unknown uuid; same text for a case the mock marks not-yours.
A signed-out 401 shows the sign-in state with `next=` the current path — verify: e2e with the mock session cleared.
A checklist read failure (mock 503 for dossier 5009) hides only the strip, shows "The closure checklist is unavailable.", and the form still saves — verify: e2e.
`meetings` returns `next_page`: the list shows "More" and loads the next page via the `page` query — verify: e2e with a 30-row fixture.
Phone width (390px) shows one column with Save reachable and tap targets at least 44px — verify: Playwright mobile project screenshot.

Against Django 8030 with a project that has `meeting.record`: first save creates the meeting, `GET /api/v1/projects/<case>/meetings?kind=retrospective` returns it, and the closure checklist `retrospective` check references the saved version — verify: curl with the session, compare to the page.

No money, no client message, no approver or count is drawn; any value the API returns as null shows as "Not recorded" or the specific wording above, never 0 or blank — verify: review of the rendered pages and `model.ts` tests for null mapping.

New tests: `summary.test.ts` (write, parse, round trip, no headings, oversize), `model.test.ts` (body builders, null handling, status words), and `retrospective.spec.ts` (criteria 1 to 20 against the mock) — verify: `npm test` and `npx playwright test e2e/retrospective.spec.ts` in `frontend/`.

risk.rationale: Medium. The screen has several behaviours (versioned save, action creation, checklist link) and a cross-layer contract: revisions, evidence ids, and a `summary` convention that decides what the screen shows. It writes internal meeting records only. No money, payroll, external messaging, auth or migrations are involved, and nothing is hard to undo because saves append versions. Surfaces are ui, api and contract-change (the three-box to one-summary packing). Product acceptance is required for the changed form layout and the hidden draft.

findings.summary: A 422 with no mappable field is not shown. Spec: "422 shows `fields[].message` under the named field, else the `message` in a `Callout`." `failureOf` (`useRetrospective.ts:33-38`) puts any field name outside `FIELD_OF` into `fields.other`, and the message becomes "Check the highlighted fields." only when some field exists. Two results. (a) `ActionForm.tsx:62` draws the Callout only when `failure.kind !== 'invalid'`, and no control reads `fields.other` or `ownerId`, so a 422 with `fields: []` (a plain `message`) or with an `owner_id` field draws nothing, and the person sees Create re-enable with no explanation. (b) `RetroForm.tsx:166-177` shows "Check the highlighted fields." when the only field was `other`, `ownerId` or `dueAt`-like and nothing is highlighted. Expected: show the API `message`, or the unplaced field messages, in the Callout whenever no control carries them; add an Owner error too. Add a test: 422 with empty `fields` on action create, and a 422 naming an unmapped field on save.

findings.summary: Phone Save bar is inside the Panel frame and is not screen-width. Expected (SCR-33-mobile.dc.html, bottom element of the 390 screen): a white bar, edge to edge, 2px top rule, padding 12/16/18, with Save full width at the foot of the screen. findings.summary: Desktop Tab order now differs from screen order. The Decisions block is before the Save row in the DOM (`RetroForm.tsx:154` and `:193`), but on desktop Save is shown above Decisions (`retrospective.css:61-62`). A keyboard user going from Notes file reaches Decision 1 and Add a decision before Save, though Save is visually directly under the notes file. Nothing is unreachable or trapped, so this is a WCAG 2.4.3 watch item, not a blocking breach. Any DOM order fixes one viewport and breaks the other, because the phone bar is last in DOM. Product/UX should decide whether the board's desktop order or the Tab order wins; the builder's note records the same trade-off.

`.retro__page { padding-bottom: 140px }` (`retrospective.css:51`) is a fixed allowance, not measured against the bar. When Save is disabled, `.psl-reason` (`Button.tsx:119-120`) sits inside the bar. The longest retro reason is about 90 characters, which wraps to two lines at 390px. That keeps the bar near 130-136px, just inside 140px. A longer reason would let the bar cover the last field at scroll end. Consider 160px or a measured spacer.

Phone (390): the fixed Save bar covers focused controls. Expected: a control that receives keyboard focus is scrolled fully above the bar (WCAG 2.4.11). Actual: after Tab or focus() the "Tunde Bello" checkbox sits at y 824-844 with the bar at 735-844, and elementFromPoint at its centre returns the bar (fully obscured). "Lessons for next projects" (708-775) is partly under the bar. Browsers only scroll into view within the full viewport, so the bar hides the element. Path: `frontend/src/features/retrospective/retrospective.css` (phone `.retro__savebar` fixed bar, `.retro__page` padding); suggested fix: set `scroll-padding-bottom` on the form or page at phone width to the bar height plus a margin (about 130px), so focus scrolls above it, and re-check the Tab walk.

Suggested fix: keep Save before Decisions in the DOM at all widths, and keep the phone bar fixed so its screen position at the foot is unchanged; or keep the phone order and make the desktop order match the DOM. findings.summary: `retrospective.css` sets `html:has(.retro__savebar) { scroll-padding-bottom: 110px }`, but the fixed bar is `padding 12 / 18`, a 2px border, a 50px Save and, when Save is disabled, a `.psl-reason` line (`Button.tsx:119-120`, rendered inside the bar). One reason line gives about 108px; two lines (the 90-character retro reason at 390px, see TECH-4-2) give about 126px. At 110px a control brought into view by focus can have its lower 16px under the bar. Expected: scroll padding at least the bar's worst case, e.g. 140px to match `.retro__page { padding-bottom: 140px }`, or measured in JS. Path: `retrospective.css:54`.

`e2e/retrospective.spec.ts` "a focused control is never hidden under the bar" focuses the Ada Obi checkbox and the Lessons field at load, where they are likely above the bar, so no scroll happens and the `scroll-padding` rule is not exercised. The test would also pass without that rule. Expected: add a case that focuses a control below the fold (the last decision or Save after scrolling) and asserts its bottom is at or above the bar's top. Path: `e2e/retrospective.spec.ts:~412-428`. The fixed `waitForTimeout(200)` is also a timing dependency; prefer waiting for the focus state.

`RetroForm.tsx:~196` switches between `<>{decisions}{saveBar}</>` and `<>{saveBar}{decisions}</>`, so both blocks remount when the viewport crosses 720px. Values survive because they are held in `draft`, but keyboard focus inside Decisions or on Save is lost on resize. Expected: accept as a known trade-off, or keep one stable order and use CSS for the bar only if the layout allows. Not a regression from the removed `order` rules.

Phone (390): the focused "Lessons for next projects" field is still under the fixed Save bar. Expected: a focused control is scrolled fully clear of the bar (WCAG 2.4.11, AA, in the e2e axe tags). Actual: Tab from "What didn't" (and focus()) leaves scrollY 0 with the field at y 708-775 and the bar top at 735; elementFromPoint at the field centre (741) returns the bar. The computed `scroll-padding-bottom` is 110px on html, so the rule applies, but Chrome does not scroll because the field is already inside the viewport. It reproduces with and without touch emulation and on projects 2001 and 5001. The builder's e2e check passes, so it does not catch this state. Path: `frontend/src/features/retrospective/retrospective.css` (phone `.retro__savebar`, `html:has(.retro__savebar)` rule). Suggested fix: give the form or page enough bottom space and scroll the focused control with `scrollIntoView({block:'nearest'})` on focus at phone width. Or add a `focusin` handler that scrolls the target above the bar's top. Re-check at scroll 0 on a fresh load, where the Lessons field starts partly hidden.
